Creative Front-End Engineer / Interaction Engineer
Posted 4 days ago

Only freelancers located in the U.S. may apply.

Send a proposal for: 26 Connects
Available Connects: 114
Summary

We are developing an AI-powered educational platform and are looking for a creative, technically strong front-end engineer to join our designer and software engineer.

We need someone who can work confidently within an established codebase, build polished and intuitive interactions, and improve the performance and reliability of the product. This includes sophisticated UI such as realistic notebook page-flipping, as well as diagnosing loading and latency issues across multiple integrations.

Our stack includes TypeScript/React, Vercel, Supabase, Clerk, Stripe, Anthropic, and Resend. Experience with these specific services is helpful but not required.

Responsibilities
- Build responsive, production-ready UI within an existing codebase
- Translate designs into polished animations, gestures, transitions, and interactions
- Diagnose and improve loading, latency, and performance across the application and external integrations
- Build secure user flows involving authentication, accounts, payments, and user data
- Ensure smooth performance across desktop and mobile
- Collaborate closely with our designer and software engineer

What We're Looking For
- Strong React and modern front-end development skills
- Experience working with established production codebases
- Experience with APIs, asynchronous data loading, and performance optimization
- Familiarity with authentication and web application security best practices
- Strong eye for interaction design, motion, and UI polish
- Ability to independently investigate and solve problems across systems
- Experience with page-turning, gesture-based interfaces, complex web animation, or similarly sophisticated interactions is especially welcome.

To Apply
Please send relevant portfolio examples, briefly describe your role and technical contribution to each, and include your availability and rate.
